blocks.text:
On this trip, city tours give way to national parks, a cable car ride, walks beside the waterfalls and a relaxing seaside stay.

## How the journey changes along the way

In São Paulo, the day revolves around the city’s contrasts. Historic squares, the cathedral, market and theatre give way to Avenida Paulista, Ibirapuera Park, residential neighbourhoods and modern architecture. You get a sense of both the old centre and the metropolis today.

At Iguazu, nature takes centre stage. The origins of the falls are linked to a volcanic eruption and shifts in the Earth’s crust. The Brazilian side gives you a clear view of the overall shape of the cascades, while on the Argentine side walkways take you directly above the rushing water and towards the Devil’s Throat from another direction.

Rio changes the mood of the trip again. Urca and Sugar Loaf offer views of the coastline, while the route up Corcovado passes through Tijuca, one of the largest tropical forests within a city. After 2 days of tours in Rio, the transfer to Búzios provides a natural pause. The resort grew from a fishing village and is known for its beaches, clear water and combination of sea, rocks and tropical vegetation.

## Trip highlights

São Paulo offers an in-depth introduction to the largest city on the route: from the cathedral, markets and old squares to Avenida Paulista, Ibirapuera Park and modern architecture.

You spend 2 days at Iguazu to see the falls from both sides of the border. The Brazilian side is especially good for panoramic views of the cascades; on the Argentine side, paths and walkways bring you much closer to the water. You can add the Bird Park and Macuco Safari if you wish.

In Rio, the programme centres on the city’s 2 main heights: Sugar Loaf and Corcovado. The route then heads to the ocean and continues to Búzios, where the active part of the journey gives way to several days relaxing on the beaches.
